cells.tense: The judgment is in your hands at this moment, and it is already warm from being held.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Set down one arrangement between people — a rule, a habit, a standing way of splitting something — that fit once and doesn't now. Don't pick it up again this week. Watch what still stands without your hand on it.
cells.core:
Someone brings you a tangle of feeling between two people and you go all the way down into it, and the call comes out of that descent, not over it. No one is sentenced for having a feeling. No one's feeling tips the scale. That works, and it works because you paid in full. What also happens: you keep handing out the same shape long after the situation it fit has changed underneath. The container that once held things open is holding them shut, and you are last to feel it move.

The fix isn't effort. It's one ending — a rule, a habit, a standing way of splitting something, fit once and doesn't now. Set it down on your side and don't pick it up again this week. The comfort of honouring it one more season is the whole cost, and the people inside already know. What opens once the old pattern stops working on them?
cells.sheetLine: You feel it all, then call it fair — and the call outlasts the field.
cells.verb: judging the emotion rightly, giving feeling its hour and calling the thing fair in the end
cells.place: the place in a life where you build the frame that holds the mess

cells.tense: You will have made the ruling before the hurt has finished arriving.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Let one hurt that reaches you this week stay unresolved for a day. Carry it as a builder carries a stone set aside for a wall not yet raised — solid, quiet, no verdict inside the weight.
cells.core:
Somebody is hurt, and before the hurt is all the way out, its shape is already in your hands: proportionate, not proportionate, whose turn, what the rule should be. The fairness is real. It just gets there before the feeling it means to hold does, and the people under it don't hear fairness — they hear a door closing mid-sentence.

A wall goes up on dry mortar, not wet. Let one hurt that reaches you this week stay unresolved for a day. Carry it as a builder carries a stone set aside for a wall not yet raised. Solid, quiet, no verdict inside it. The judgment doesn't have to be slow forever; it has to be slow enough to be about the thing it rules on. What does a hurt say in its second day that it couldn't in its first?
cells.sheetLine: You've already ruled before the hurt has finished being felt.
cells.verb: judging the emotion rightly, giving feeling its hour and calling the thing fair in the end
cells.place: the place in a life where you build the frame that holds the mess

cells.tense: The saying of unfairness stopped, and the quiet since has become the tone of the place.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Write one unfair situation out in order — this, then this, then this — in plain words, no feeling on the page. Read it back once. No decision waiting at the end, only the record.
cells.core:
You can still see where things between people are out of proportion. That part didn't go. What went is the step from seeing to saying, from the shelf to the pen. The imbalance sits where it landed, the people around it feel the lean, and whoever could have fixed it has stepped back from the bench. It reads as not caring. It is closer to not having the next motion in the hand.

Method can go where nerve won't. Write one unfair situation out in order — this, then this, then this — in plain words, no feeling on the page, and read it back once. Nothing has to be decided and nobody has to be told. The facts just need to be somewhere your eye can meet them, and the call tends to arrive half-made, in your own handwriting. What does the page say that the room couldn't?
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's unfair, and the saying of it stopped.
cells.verb: judging the emotion rightly, giving feeling its hour and calling the thing fair in the end
cells.place: the place in a life where you build the frame that holds the mess

cells.tense: The balance between the people near you is being held, and your own telling has you standing outside it.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: At the next argument you're near, hear the whole of it through before you make your usual small correction. Not as the one who settles it, but as someone learning it for the first time. See what lands that usually gets smoothed over.
cells.core:
A word placed here, a quiet refusal to take a side there, a weight shifted while nobody's watching — the balance around you holds, and your telling of it says you were only present. That telling is real to you. Those who have been kept level have not quite bought it, and they don't have to; they can feel the hand under the table.

Nothing needs announcing. The work needs to be seen from inside. At the next argument you're near, hear the whole of it through first, as someone learning it for the first time, before you make your usual small correction. Don't tune anything. Don't reach for the level. Let the hearing be the whole act. The part you normally smooth over will arrive before anything has smoothed it. What does the keeper's work look like when the keeper is watching it happen?
cells.sheetLine: You keep the balance between people and say you're just standing there.
cells.verb: judging the emotion rightly, giving feeling its hour and calling the thing fair in the end
cells.place: the place in a life where you build the frame that holds the mess
